pdpl.subtitle: Based on the Personal Data Protection Law No. 91/2025/QH15 (effective 01/01/2026) and Decree 356/2025/ND-CP

pdpl.coverageIntro: The report only has data from modules that are on:
pdpl.regimeNote: Your size and the traits you declared decide this item: small enterprises and startups may choose to comply or not during those 5 years, micro enterprises and household businesses need not comply (Article 38 of the Law; Article 41 of Decree 356/2025/ND-CP). Not mandatory does not mean not advisable.
pdpl.levelNote: The information system security level falls under separate rules, not the Personal Data Protection Law; shown as you declared it.
basis: Personal Data Protection Law No. 91/2025/QH15, effective 01/01/2026.
Decree 356/2025/ND-CP of 31/12/2025 guiding the Law (Official Gazette No. 18, 18/01/2026), replacing Decree 13/2023/ND-CP.

Decree article numbers were checked directly against the Gazette text; Law article numbers against the full text on legal databases. The texts may be amended or supplemented: check the current version before filing.
The information system security level falls under the 2025 Cybersecurity Law (effective 01/07/2026) and its guidance, outside this report.

dpia.title: Personal data processing impact assessment dossier
dpia.body: Prepare and keep the dossier from the day processing starts; file 1 original with the specialized agency (under the Ministry of Public Security) within 60 days of starting processing, with Form 02a or 02b. Update every 6 months when something changes, or within 10 days on reorganisation, dissolution or a change of data protection service provider (Law Articles 21, 22; Decree 356 Articles 19, 20). Vedette supplies the technical figures in the sections above; the person in charge writes the legal part.

dpo.title: Person or unit in charge of personal data protection
dpo.body: Appoint in writing, stating assignment, functions and authority, or hire a provider of data protection services (Law Article 33(2)). Staff need at least a college degree, 2 years of relevant experience and data protection training (Decree 356 Article 13). This report records the person you entered in the form; Vedette does not check the appointment document.

breach.title: Procedure when a data breach happens
breach.body: On detecting a breach likely to harm national defense, public order and safety, or a data subject's life, health, honor, dignity or property, notify the specialized agency within 72 hours of detection, using Form 08 or the national portal, and keep a written record (Law Article 23; Decree 356 Article 28). For location and biometric data you must also notify data subjects within 72 hours and keep breach records for at least 5 years (Decree 356 Article 29). Vedette reports technical detections but never notifies any authority by itself.

consent.title: Consent and data subject rights
consent.body: Consent must be voluntary, explicit and specific to each purpose, and capable of being printed or copied to text; silence or no response is not consent (Law Article 9). Keep proof of consent and bear the burden of proof in a dispute (Decree 356 Article 6). You need a process for data subject requests: respond within 2 working days; act on withdrawal of consent within 15 days, access or correction within 10 days, deletion within 20 days, with one extension (Decree 356 Article 5). This is outside what Vedette can see.

sensitive.title: Sensitive personal data
sensitive.body: You declared that you process sensitive data (list in Decree 356 Article 4). You need access rules, processing procedures and security measures (Article 4(2)); when asking for consent you must say that the data is sensitive (Article 6(4)). Organisations that directly process sensitive data get no exemption or option to skip the impact dossier and the data protection person (Decree 356 Article 41).

cross_border.title: Transfer of data abroad
cross_border.body: You declared that you transfer data abroad. You must prepare a cross-border transfer impact assessment dossier (report on Form 09) and file 1 original with Form 01a or 01b with the specialized agency within 60 days of starting the transfer (Law Article 20; Decree 356 Article 18). Some cases are exempt, for example HR management under labor rules, payments, logistics, visa applications (Decree 356 Article 17(3)). Small and micro enterprises are not exempt from this duty under Article 41.

processors.title: Outsourced data processors
processors.body: You need a contract or agreement stating each party's responsibilities, rights and obligations; a processor only receives data after signing and must process per the contract and apply protection measures (Law Article 37). Contracts with cloud services have extra requirements, including encryption at rest and in transit (Decree 356 Article 12).
